summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted with chest pain that began after dialysis. The pain was sharp, worse with exertion, and accompanied by nausea, diarrhea, and muscle cramps. Initial evaluation showed transient hypotension after nitroglycerin, EKG changes without cardiac enzyme elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction. The chest pain was determined to be atypical and likely related to a viral illness and chest wall inflammation, with improvement on ibuprofen. He also experienced lightheadedness, attributed to hypovolemia from recent illness and dialysis. His blood pressure stabilized, and cardiac medications were resumed. He underwent scheduled hemodialysis during admission and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all medications, including an increased dose of sevelamer, and to follow up with his cardiologist.
problems: End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
